answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can post bids or claim rewards. The protocol links the bond to a rate-limited bridge from verified deposits, so creating a thousand identities means funding a thousand independent locks, not merely changing names. If an account double-claims or colludes in a provable way, its bond is forfeited to affected users. A raven can still copy behavior, and quartz can still be cheap; neither makes the required capital free. The defense raises Sybil costs rather than proving every agent is unique.
